create.title: Create knowledge path
create.fundInstead: To have the community fund it with Bitcoin Cash,
create.error: Could not create the knowledge path
create.coverHint: Recommended: a 16:9 image for the best display.
create.guideTitle: How do you create a good path?
create.guideLead: Creating a knowledge path is an exercise in clarity: you are designing the ideal route for someone else to approach a topic step by step.
create.journey1: • In what order should someone approach this topic?
create.journey2: • Are there different levels of complexity for this topic?
create.journey3: • How can they move forward step by step?
create.notJustTitle: It is more than grouping content:
create.notJustBody: A good path is not a list of links. It is a learning experience: each node prepares the next one.
create.questions1: • If you knew nothing about this topic, what would come first?
create.questions2: • Which pieces of content are gems on this topic, and what makes someone ready to appreciate them?
create.closing: Imagine you are designing the ideal map for someone who wants to learn this without getting frustrated or wasting time.

funding.draftConnectTitle: Connect the wallet that pays the opening fee
funding.draftConnectBody: Connecting does not spend Bitcoin Cash. Next you will choose where the raised funds are paid. Only after that will the wallet ask you to approve the miner fee.
funding.draftWaitingTitle: Approve the connection in the wallet
funding.draftWaitingBody: Open the wallet and allow this page to read its addresses. Nothing is spent.
funding.draftNeedBody: Send at least {{sats}} satoshis to the fee wallet below, then check again.
funding.feeWalletNote: This address pays the miner fee. It does not receive the raised funds.
funding.receiveStepBody: This is where the raised Bitcoin Cash is paid when the investigation is claimed. Enter it now. The opening payment records this address, so it is chosen before the wallet approves anything. Any {{prefix}}: address works.
funding.openStepBody: The wallet will ask you to approve one payment. That payment creates the crowdfunding coin and pays the miner fee. This page then publishes it to the Bitcoin Cash network. Nothing is sent until you approve. The raised Bitcoin Cash will be paid to the receive address below.
funding.openStepBodyTwo: The wallet will ask twice. The first approval moves your coins so the investigation can start. This page publishes that payment. The second approval creates the crowdfunding coin and pays the miner fee. This page publishes that payment too. Nothing is sent until you approve each one.
funding.approveMove: Approve the first payment in the wallet. It moves your coins so the investigation can start. This page will publish it after you approve.
funding.publishingMove: The first payment is signed. Publishing it to the Bitcoin Cash network, then waiting until the network can see it.
funding.approveOpen: Approve the opening payment in the wallet. It creates the crowdfunding coin and pays the miner fee.
funding.publishingOpen: The opening payment is signed. Publishing it to the Bitcoin Cash network, then waiting until the network can see it.
funding.notPublished: The wallet approved the payment, but the Bitcoin Cash network does not have it yet. The coins are still in the fee wallet.
funding.broadcastRejected: The Bitcoin Cash network rejected the signed payment. The coins are still in the fee wallet.
funding.draftWalletRestored: This browser restored the WizardConnect session from the last time you paired a wallet. Disconnect if you want to pair again.
funding.walletUnreadable: The wallet connected, but this page could not read its addresses. Disconnect and try again.
funding.draftClosed: This investigation is not open for funding yet.
funding.walletHelp: Connect your wallet with Wizard Connect and press Pledge. Only that Wizard Connect transaction counts as a pledge. Sending Bitcoin Cash to an address does not.
funding.walletHelpClosed: Connect the Wizard Connect wallet that made the pledge. If that pledge is confirmed, you can reclaim the pledge.
funding.pledgeHow: A pledge works only through Wizard Connect. The connected wallet signs it, adds the satoshis to the crowdfunding coin, and keeps the receipt. A Bitcoin Cash payment you send on your own does not count, and its transaction id cannot be recorded here.
funding.pledgeWalletNote: This wallet holds the receipt for a pledge made from it. It does not hold the crowdfunding coin, and it does not receive the raised funds.
funding.recordHelp: Paste the transaction id from that Wizard Connect pledge so Academia Blockchain can index it. A Bitcoin Cash payment sent without Wizard Connect does not count, and recording its transaction id does not make it a pledge.
funding.supportHelp: This message goes to Academia Blockchain support and includes this investigation.
funding.supportError: The message could not be sent.
funding.claimed: The pool was claimed. The raised Bitcoin Cash is paid to the payout address.
funding.expireHelp: The goal was not reached. Close pledges before a pledge can be reclaimed. The wallet pays the miner fee. A new pledge is no longer possible after this.
funding.expired: Pledges are closed. A confirmed pledge can now be reclaimed.
funding.noCoin: The connected wallet {{address}} does not have {{sats}} satoshis yet. Send at least {{sats}} satoshis to that wallet address and try again once the payment arrives.
funding.preparingOpen: The wallet will ask twice. The first approval moves your coins into a payment this investigation can start from. The second opens it.
funding.needGenesisCoin: This address already has {{sats}} satoshis, so the coins are not still on the way. That payment cannot open the investigation because it is not the first output of its transaction. Send more than 3,000 satoshis to this address as the only recipient, then try again.
funding.accessTitle: This path was funded with Bitcoin Cash
funding.accessBody: The finished knowledge path is open to everyone.
